article.title: Arch package guidelines
article.access: wikiman -R -s arch -l en; local HTML read with w3m -dump
article.page_last_edited: 2026-05-02 (as shown in local page footer; not the access date)

scope.analysis: read-only comparison; no package build attempted

evidence.decision_summary: PKGBUILD uses several sound Arch conventions (local package data in /usr/lib/prime-agent, executable entry point under /usr/bin, SPDX MIT plus installed license, underscore-prefixed helper variable, version cross-check). Key unresolved review areas are direct runtime/build dependencies, optional features, source provenance/reproducibility of a deliberately local-checkout package, and validating the produced package with namcap/reproducible-build tools. These are review items, not blanket findings of non-compliance.

guidance.topic: Function roles, package tree, and file modes

wiki.text: Makepkg builds and installs software into a fake root, then creates the package archive. Use standard locations: executables in /usr/bin, modules/plugins in /usr/lib/pkg, application data in /usr/share/pkg, documentation in /usr/share/doc/pkg, and licenses in /usr/share/licenses/pkg. Never install to /usr/local; avoid /usr/libexec. Quote variables that may contain spaces. The page recommends an .install file for important install-time messages or required setup.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: prepare stages a source tree, build installs/builds there, check runs the bundled CLI --version, and package places deployed files below $pkgdir/usr/lib/prime-agent, installs LICENSE below $pkgdir/usr/share/licenses/prime-agent, and symlinks /usr/bin/prime-agent to the CLI. It chmods the CLI 755 and uses install -m644/-Dm644 for files. No .install file is declared.
guidance.assessment: Paths and explicit executable/license modes fit the listed conventions. No .install file is needed unless package setup or important post-install guidance is required. Verify the final package tree; the source code alone cannot prove every deployed file has suitable modes or no forbidden path.
checks: Inspect package contents with bsdtar -tf <package>.
Run namcap <package> and review permission/path warnings.
Check that the installed symlink resolves to an executable file; confirm packaged data and licenses are under the intended /usr paths.

guidance.topic: PKGBUILD names, custom variables, output, and description

wiki.text: Do not introduce variables/functions unless needed; prefix required additions with underscore to avoid collisions with makepkg. Do not call makepkg helper routines such as msg/error; use printf or echo. Keep descriptions self-referencing-free and about 80 characters or less, and lines roughly below 100 characters. Quote variables such as $pkgdir and $srcdir where spaces may occur.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: The helper `_repo_root` is underscore-prefixed and needed to locate the documented parent checkout. Error reporting uses printf. Paths generally quote $srcdir/$pkgdir. pkgdesc is descriptive and under the suggested length. Standard makepkg phases are used; no custom PKGBUILD function appears.
guidance.assessment: The inspected examples follow these recommendations. Line length is a style check, not evidence of a build failure.
checks: Run shellcheck --shell=bash --exclude=SC2034,SC2154,SC2164 PKGBUILD (command is mentioned by the related PKGBUILD page, not Arch package guidelines).
Review custom variable/function names and quoting during PKGBUILD review.

wiki.text: pkgver should match the version released by the upstream author. pkgrel starts at 1 for a new upstream version, increments for package-only fixes/optimizations, and resets to 1 when upstream releases a new version. The page also gives restrictions for version characters and replacing upstream hyphens with underscores.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: pkgver=0.9.8, pkgrel=1. prepare reads packages/coding-agent/package.json and fails if that version differs from pkgver.
guidance.assessment: The local version guard helps avoid a stale package version. It checks the checkout metadata, not independently whether that checkout is an official upstream release. pkgrel=1 is appropriate only if this is the first packaging release for this pkgver.
checks: Compare package.json version with the upstream release/tag selected for the build.
On package-only edits at fixed pkgver, increment pkgrel; reset pkgrel when pkgver changes.

guidance.topic: Runtime dependencies, build dependencies, optional features

wiki.text: Do not rely on transitive dependencies. List direct library dependencies. Carefully verify dependencies using executable/script requirements and documentation; the page recommends ldd, ldd --unused --function-relocs, readelf dynamic information, and namcap. Dependencies for optional functionality should normally be optdepends with a short feature description, not hard depends. The PKGBUILD page distinguishes runtime depends, build-only makedepends, and test-only checkdepends; test dependencies are relevant when check() runs.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: depends=(nodejs>=22.8.0 python>=3.11 uv); makedepends=(pnpm rsync); optdepends=(). check() invokes Node on the bundled CLI with --version. build() runs pnpm install and pnpm run build. package() uses pnpm deploy --prod and --ignore-scripts.
guidance.assessment: The split between declared runtime and packaging/build tools is structurally reasonable. Whether the set is complete is unverified. In a Node/Rust/Python mixed application, inspect actual runtime imports, invoked commands, native shared objects/addons, and feature gates. Rust/Cargo/compiler packages are build dependencies only if build actually compiles Rust from source; prebuilt artifacts or skipped optional modules change that conclusion. Do not add them solely because the repository contains Rust. Identify optional features before keeping optdepends empty. The version floor on Node should match actual upstream/runtime needs.
checks: Review built scripts and runtime configuration for invoked commands and Python modules; test in a clean install containing only declared runtime dependencies.
Use ldd -u -r or ldd --unused --function-relocs on applicable native executables; use readelf -d for dynamic dependencies. These do not discover every JS/Python-level dependency.
Use namcap on both PKGBUILD and resulting package; inspect its findings rather than treating it as proof of completeness.
Determine from the locked dependency graph/build logs whether any crate/native addon is compiled from source, then classify its tools as makedepends and runtime libraries as depends.
If tests need extra packages beyond depends/makedepends, declare checkdepends; run makepkg's check phase in the intended build workflow.

guidance.topic: Sources, checksums, signatures, source uniqueness, provenance

wiki.text: Prefer HTTPS for tarballs and git sources. Verify sources with PGP signatures wherever possible. Preserve security/integrity checks; use unique source filenames in srcdir/SRCDEST; avoid specific mirrors likely to disappear. The article's suggested pinned Git-tag object-hash approach is explicitly marked disputed for factual accuracy, with a note that recent pacman supports proper checksums for Git sources.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: source=() and sha256sums=(). prepare copies the live parent checkout into $srcdir using rsync and excludes selected directories. The comment explicitly says it packages the parent checkout, not an unrelated upstream tag.
guidance.assessment: This is a deliberately local-checkout PKGBUILD rather than a makepkg-fetched release-source recipe. That explains the empty arrays, so they are not by themselves proof of a violation for this local workflow. Inference: package provenance and repeatability depend on the caller's checkout state and are not authenticated/pinned by source/checksum metadata. If the recipe is published or expected to build independently, prefer a fixed release source with appropriate integrity/signature checks. Treat the Git object-hash example cautiously because the Wiki flags that guidance as disputed.
checks: For distributable recipe use, define a versioned HTTPS source or justified VCS source; ensure source filenames are unique and checksums/signatures correspond to the exact selected revision.
For the local-checkout workflow, record the checkout revision/status in the build release process and check that prepare excludes only intended data.
Do not present the empty source/checksum arrays as a proven defect without first deciding whether this local-only package recipe is intended to be independently reproducible.

wiki.text: Arch is working toward reproducible packages. The page recommends makerepropkg (devtools) or repro (archlinux-repro) to check a built package. If a build-time timestamp is required, use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: The PKGBUILD does not itself document a reproducibility check or SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH handling. pnpm install/build and a live-checkout source are relevant inputs to verify.
guidance.assessment: Absence of these commands in PKGBUILD is not proof the resulting package is non-reproducible. A live working tree and changing dependency/network state make repeatability a meaningful question. No package was rebuilt for this review.
checks: After a package is available, run makerepropkg <package-file> or repro -f <package-file> in the documented environment.
If timestamps affect outputs, propagate/use SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH; investigate non-deterministic generated files and dependency-fetch behavior.

wiki.text: Use arch=('any') only when the package is architecture-independent after building. An architecture-specific compiled package should declare supported architectures, e.g. x86_64.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: arch=('x86_64'); package() retains the koffi linux_x64 subtree and prunes other platform directories.
guidance.assessment: The x86_64 declaration is consistent with the native-addon clue. Confirm all bundled native code/addons have the same support boundary; do not change to any merely because most application files are JS/Python text.
checks: Inventory native binaries and addon prebuilds in the package; confirm x86_64 is the actual supported target and that pruning does not remove required runtime files.

wiki.chapter: Licenses — PKGBUILD's license field; Licenses — Package sources licenses; Directories
wiki.text: The license field represents the packaged upstream software and uses SPDX identifiers. The corresponding license text belongs under /usr/share/licenses/pkgname. Separately, the page states Arch package-source contributions use 0BSD for the packaging source and REUSE.toml/pkgctl license check under the cited Arch RFCs; this source-license rule is distinct from the upstream software license.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: license=('MIT'); package() installs the repository LICENSE to /usr/share/licenses/prime-agent/LICENSE with mode 644.
guidance.assessment: The field and destination align in form; verify that upstream licensing is indeed MIT and that LICENSE is the correct text. If submitting packaging sources under the Arch package-source policy, review that separate source-license/REUSE requirement; do not replace the software's MIT license field with 0BSD on that account.
checks: Verify upstream license and exact packaged license text; inspect namcap output.
For an Arch packaging-source submission, check required packaging-source license metadata separately, including REUSE/pkgctl license check as stated by the Wiki.

wiki.text: Do not list the package itself in provides or conflicts; external shared libraries may be listed in provides when applicable. Put nonessential feature dependencies in optdepends with a short feature description.

guidance.pkgbuild_observation: provides/conflicts are not declared; optdepends is empty.
guidance.assessment: No relation entry is required merely to repeat the package's own name. Empty optdepends is suitable only if no optional functionality should be described; the feature audit remains outstanding.
checks: Review CLI feature documentation/configuration and identify optional integrations; add only real nonessential package dependencies with feature descriptions if relevant.
Do not add prime-agent to its own provides/conflicts arrays.

non_wiki_build_obstacle.reported_fact: Parent specified an already-confirmed build obstacle: postinstall.cjs is missing.
non_wiki_build_obstacle.classification: Build/repository fact, not a rule in Arch package guidelines.
non_wiki_build_obstacle.implication: It can prevent validating the packaging build independently of any Arch packaging-policy assessment. Do not attribute it to the Wiki or infer a packaging-rule violation from it.
non_wiki_build_obstacle.verification_status: Reported as previously established by parent; this review did not retry makepkg or independently reproduce it.

important_limits: No build or package retry was performed.
This review compares the read-only PKGBUILD with the named ArchWiki article only; Node.js/Rust/Python-specific Wiki pages were not consulted.
The article says to also consult PKGBUILD(5) and makepkg(8), but those sources were outside this requested article-only evidence scope.
Recommendations/check commands above distinguish explicit Wiki statements from case-specific application and proposed checks; they are not a blanket compliance verdict.
